elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly states that the Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90) days' written notice, not thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires any refund of prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The existing language permits either Party to terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice and does not expressly restrict HDI's termination right to the end of a committed term.

elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits the Customer to terminate for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90) days' written notice, which is within the permitted range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: Although the Termination Payment is capped, the cap is based on aggregate payments made under Section 3.1 during or for the preceding three months, not expressly on fees attributable to a three-month period. Without Section 3.1 or clearer operative language, the cap could include a lump-sum or other payment exceeding three months' fees.

elements.element: Vendor has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The original clause permits either Party, including HDI, to terminate upon written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may exercise its termination-for-convenience right only effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly require HDI's specified Termination Date to coincide with the end of the initial or a renewal term.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' written notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: The mutual termination language requires either Party to give ninety (90) days' written notice.

result.reason: The redline gives Customer an express ninety-day convenience-termination right, but it omits the preferred thirty-day notice and pro-rata refund. It also fails to confine Vendor termination to a term end. The payment-based cap does not unambiguously cap the charge at fees attributable to three months. Because neither complete position is achieved, the redline is not minimal as defined, although it does not materially disturb unrelated terms or create an irreconcilable contradiction.
